sections.heading: C2 — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A44
When a stop is required, stop behind the applicable line or crosswalk; without an apparent crosswalk, stop before the intersection. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A44
Crosswalks are pedestrian crossing areas; yield to pedestrians entering or occupying them. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A44
Some crosswalks are unmarked, so watch for pedestrians at intersections. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A44
If a stop line precedes a crosswalk, stop at the line first. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A44
When leaving an alley, driveway or building across a sidewalk, stop behind the sidewalk and yield to pedestrians and traffic. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A44
A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction, not passing or through travel. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A44
Avoid entering a shared left-turn lane too early because longer exposure increases conflict with opposing users. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A44
Before entering a shared left-turn lane, check ahead, mirrors and the left blind spot, then signal and enter smoothly when safe. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A44
In a shared left-turn lane, watch traffic from driveways and side streets and choose a gap in opposing traffic. [A44]
Source: [A44 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A45
A reversible lane carries traffic in different directions at different times; check its current controls before entering. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A45
Reversible lanes may have double broken yellow boundaries and overhead lane-control signals. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A45
A green lane-control arrow permits use of the lane beneath it; a red X closes that lane. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A45
A flashing yellow X designates a turning-only lane. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A45
A steady yellow X announces a lane-use change; leave the lane as soon as safely possible. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A45
Watch for drivers entering a reversible lane from the opposing direction by mistake. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A45
Reserved lanes have signs specifying the permitted users and often a white diamond on a sign or pavement. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A45
A lane marked Transit or Bus is reserved for buses; a Bicycle lane is reserved for cyclists. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A45
HOV means High Occupancy Vehicles; posted rules may specify occupancy, days and hours. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A45
HOV 3 requires at least three occupants while the posted restriction applies. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A45
Backing in a travel lane is prohibited except for parallel parking. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A45
After missing a turn or exit, continue to a safe place to turn around rather than backing up. [A45]
Source: [A45 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A46
On a road with two or more same-direction lanes, the handbook directs drivers to stay right except when passing. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A46
On roads with at least three same-direction lanes, the handbook recommends the center travel lane, particularly around frequent entering and exiting traffic. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A46
Do not drive on the shoulder unless directed by law enforcement or permitted by local rules. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A46
The leftmost lane on a multilane road is intended for passing slower vehicles. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A46
Passing on the right can put the vehicle where another driver has difficulty seeing it before changing lanes. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A46
Never use the shoulder to pass, whether the shoulder is paved or unpaved. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A46
Before a turn, scan every corner for controls, pedestrians and vehicles, and signal the intended movement. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A46
Without signs or markings directing otherwise, approach a turn in the lane nearest the intended direction. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A46
Recheck traffic, look along the intended path and steer smoothly through a turn. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A46
As a safety precaution, turn into the closest lane traveling in the desired direction to minimize crossed lanes. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A46
After a turn, accelerate smoothly, cancel the signal, check behind and move right when safe if necessary. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A46
Avoid swinging left before a right turn because a following driver may try to pass on the right. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R34 | anchor: A46
Make a right turn from the rightmost lane unless markings permit simultaneous turns from multiple lanes. [A46]
Source: [A46 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R35 | anchor: A47
For a left turn, avoid cutting across the corner into the path of traffic approaching from the left. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R36 | anchor: A47
Leave room for opposing vehicles to turn left in front of the vehicle. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R37 | anchor: A47
Turn left from the leftmost lane unless markings permit multiple left-turn lanes. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R38 | anchor: A47
For multiple turning lanes, identify and enter the needed lane at least one block before turning, after mirror and blind-spot checks and a signal. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R39 | anchor: A47
When safe on green, maintain the corresponding lane through a multilane turn and accelerate smoothly. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R40 | anchor: A47
The handbook's safest direction reversal is a right turn followed by travel around the block, avoiding most left turns across traffic. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R41 | anchor: A47
On an interstate, continue to the next exit to reverse direction. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R42 | anchor: A47
Crossing an interstate median or using an emergency-vehicle crossover is illegal. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R43 | anchor: A48
A two-point turnabout uses a driveway, alley or street when circling a block is impractical or impossible. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R44 | anchor: A48
Backing into a driveway is the safer two-point method because it improves the view when leaving; use this maneuver only on a two-lane road. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R45 | anchor: A48
For a reverse two-point turn, signal right, stop and check beside and behind the vehicle before backing toward the driveway. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

Misconceptions: A green light still requires a clear intersection; no-passing markings differ from turn permissions; a painted center lane is not a physical bus-stop barrier.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: control, clear path, correct lane, complete maneuver. It adds no right-of-way entitlement.
Glossary: Distinguish crossbuck, ENS, reversible lane, HOV lane, shared left-turn lane and physical median using the sourced facts.
Dynamic facts: Signs, local restrictions and edition-bound legal distances require issuer rechecking when this source is superseded; unresolved sign visuals and wording remain typed debt.

sections.heading: C2 — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-R46 | anchor: A48
In the reverse two-point procedure, start the rightward backing turn when the rear bumper reaches the driveway's near edge. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R47 | anchor: A48
When centered in the driveway during a reverse two-point turn, straighten the wheels and stop; select drive, check both ways and turn left only when clear after signaling. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R48 | anchor: A48
For a forward two-point turn, check mirrors, signal left and turn from near the road center into the right side of the driveway or alley. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R49 | anchor: A48
In a forward two-point turn, stop after the rear clears the road edge; check all directions, signal right and select reverse. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R50 | anchor: A48
Back slowly out of the forward two-point setup only with a clear path, steering right; once centered in the nearest lane, straighten, stop, select drive and cancel the signal. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R51 | anchor: A48
The handbook calls the three-point turnabout its most difficult and dangerous reversal; use it only on a two-lane road too narrow for a U-turn when circling the block is impossible. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R52 | anchor: A48
Begin a three-point turn by checking mirrors, signaling right and stopping at the road's right side. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R53 | anchor: A48
For the first crossing of a three-point turn, signal left and check traffic and the left blind spot; when clear, steer hard left and stop across the road. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R54 | anchor: A48
For the reverse leg of a three-point turn, check traffic and both blind spots; when clear, reverse with a hard right turn and stop. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R55 | anchor: A48
For the final leg of a three-point turn, select drive, signal left and check traffic and blind spots; when clear, turn left into the new direction's right lane and ensure signal cancellation. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R56 | anchor: A49
U-turns need sufficient turning room and are not permitted everywhere; obey signs prohibiting them. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R57 | anchor: A49
Before a permitted U-turn, wait for a large gap in both directions and watch vehicles turning right into the intended path. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R58 | anchor: A49
Roundabout traffic moves counterclockwise around a raised island, and entering vehicles yield to circulating traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R59 | anchor: A49
The handbook recommends slowing to about 15 to 20 mph for the sharp curve at roundabout entry. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R60 | anchor: A49
Choose the correct roundabout lane before entry, follow signs and markings to the exit, and do not change lanes or pass inside. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R61 | anchor: A49
Yield to roundabout pedestrians and cyclists; the handbook also tells simultaneous arrivals to yield to a vehicle on the right. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R62 | anchor: A49
Enter the circle to the right and then follow its counterclockwise path. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R63 | anchor: A50
For a rightward roundabout movement, signal right on approach and keep signaling until after the exit. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R64 | anchor: A50
For a straight-through roundabout movement, no approach signal is needed; signal right before the chosen exit. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R65 | anchor: A50
For a leftward roundabout movement, the handbook directs a right signal after traveling three quarters around, to take the exit. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R66 | anchor: A50
Avoid driving alongside trucks or buses in a roundabout. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R67 | anchor: A50
Stop for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights, an extended stop arm, or both. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R68 | anchor: A50
After the bus lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn, proceed only when safe and children have completely cleared the roadway. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R69 | anchor: A50
Two solid yellow lines do not exempt opposite-direction traffic from the school-bus stopping rule. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R70 | anchor: A51
A center turning lane does not create an opposite-direction exemption from the school-bus stopping rule. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R71 | anchor: A51
The handbook's school-bus stopping examples include multilane highways and intersections for vehicles on either side of the road. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-R72 | anchor: A52
An oncoming school bus does not require a stop when a median or another physical barrier separates the roadways. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R73 | anchor: A52
Park where the vehicle will not interfere with a travel lane and can be seen by traffic approaching from either direction. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R74 | anchor: A52
Use designated parking areas where required and park as far from traffic as possible, close to a curb when present. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R75 | anchor: A52
When parking, set the parking brake, then leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in park. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R76 | anchor: A52
Switch off headlights and the engine before taking out the key. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R77 | anchor: A52
Check mirrors and traffic before opening a vehicle door, and close the door promptly after exiting. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R78 | anchor: A52
Do not leave ignition keys in a parked vehicle; lock the doors when leaving it. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R79 | anchor: A52
To enter a vehicle parked on a street, approach its driver door from the front with the key ready so oncoming traffic is easier to observe. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R80 | anchor: A52
For downhill parking with or without a curb, stop parallel within 12 inches of the curb or road edge. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R81 | anchor: A52
For downhill parking, turn the wheels toward the curb or edge while creeping forward and stop as the tire touches the curb or reaches the edge. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R82 | anchor: A52
For uphill parking with a curb, stop parallel within 12 inches and turn the wheels away from the curb while moving slowly forward. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R83 | anchor: A52
After setting uphill-with-curb wheel direction, stop and allow a slow roll back until the tire meets the curb, then stop. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-R84 | anchor: A53
For uphill parking without a curb, stop parallel within 12 inches of the edge and turn toward the edge while creeping forward until the nearest tire reaches it. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R85 | anchor: A53
Before angle or perpendicular parking, identify the space, check traffic, signal and position away from the space to prepare the turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R86 | anchor: A53
Enter an angle or perpendicular space slowly, center the vehicle, straighten the wheels, move to the front and secure it after stopping. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0053]

sections.heading: C2 — Rules of the road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Rules of the road

FACT_ID: sec06-R87 | anchor: A53
Before backing out of an angle or perpendicular space, check traffic in every direction, hold the brake, select reverse and signal the turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R88 | anchor: A53
During the parking-space exit, continue checking traffic and back toward the intended rearward direction; stop when centered in the lane before selecting drive. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R89 | anchor: A54
Before parallel parking, check traffic and signal; let following traffic pass while stopped beside the vehicle ahead of the chosen space. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R90 | anchor: A54
With traffic clear, parallel-park by looking in the rearward path and backing slowly, first angling into the space then steering to center the vehicle. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R91 | anchor: A54
During parallel parking, stop short of the rear vehicle's bumper, then select drive to adjust the final position. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R92 | anchor: A54
Before leaving parallel parking, check traffic, use the brake and reverse carefully toward the vehicle behind to gain room. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R93 | anchor: A54
To leave parallel parking, check and signal before moving forward slowly into traffic, ensuring the front bumper clears the vehicle ahead. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R94 | anchor: A54
Do not park in an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or in a construction area where the vehicle blocks traffic. [A54]
